blocks.text: SOP: A/C and electrical accessory checks

This is the working cut for RDW-SOP-2022-055 on November 3, 2022. Tess Brant asked for a written bound after the current path (Gauge first, gas first, fuse last) stopped being honest. I am Jeilen Jones, Shop Helper, writing for Cal Dreher, Nina Soto, and Hank Morel. Primary host bay-01.ridgeway.internal. If you are skimming, jump the decision callout, then the refuse on recharge first because 'it is probably low', then open questions. If you are on the floor next shift, jump the constraints, the numbers table, and the steps.

Fuse, clutch click, then gauge. No gas on an open circuit. Accessories get the same fuse walk. I am not restating a hallway yes. recharge first because 'it is probably low' is out because October 13 recharge on an open clutch dumped $84 of gas and still blew warm. Cost of doing nothing is already in the numbers: gas=84, clutch=1, fuse=1, weeks=3, warm=1, walk=1, open=1, first=0. Sibling tickets RDW-2410 and RDW-INC-2022-041. I will not reopen recharge first because 'it is probably low' in a side thread because someone asked for a rate waiver. Nina Soto is the acceptor unless the owners line says otherwise.

blocks.text: Background. Why the current path is the wrong tool

Hank Morel owns a leftover that is easy to skip: parts.ridgeway.internal. I will ping once. After that the owner is late, not blocked. Unique to this file (37): refuse on recharge first because 'it is probably low', lock is fuse, click, then gauge, no gas on open. I will not hide a process change inside a 'quick align' on RDW-2410.
If the clutch does not click, I do not recharge. I find the open.

What a skeptical lead would try first on bay-01.ridgeway.internal: the path Tess Brant actually has, not an empty-tote photo. Metric I will argue is a clean confirm, not a vanity units-per-hour. If we cannot show that path on shop.ridgeway.internal with the numbers already in this file, we do not have a cut. Jeilen Jones will not accept a hallway yes as that proof.
